question: An API Gateway REST API receives many identical GET requests. Each cache miss invokes Lambda functions or HTTP backends that query databases, but responses can be reused for several minutes. The company wants to reduce backend invocations without changing backend code. Which solution has the least operational overhead?
options: Enable an API Gateway cache for the stage and configure caching and TTL settings for the applicable methods.
Increase the capacity of every backend Auto Scaling group.
Attach EBS volumes to the Lambda functions and store responses on the volumes.
Use Route 53 weighted records to distribute identical requests among API endpoints.
explanation:
Correct answer:
A. API Gateway REST API caching stores responses in a managed stage cache. Matching requests can be served from the cache until the configured TTL expires, reducing repeated Lambda, HTTP-backend, and database work without modifying the backend implementation.

Why the other options are wrong:
B. Additional backend capacity may increase throughput but still processes every request and can increase cost.
C. Lambda functions cannot attach EBS volumes, and EBS is not a managed API response cache.
D. Route 53 controls DNS routing and does not cache HTTP responses or eliminate backend requests.

Exam trigger:
Repeated cacheable REST API requests are creating avoidable backend executions.

Exam trap:
API Gateway stage caching applies to REST APIs; it is not the same feature set as an API Gateway HTTP API.

Memory hook:
Cache at the API stage to avoid repeating backend work.

question: A company has a predictable hourly baseline across EC2, Fargate, and Lambda. EC2 instance families, operating systems, and Regions may change during the commitment term. Which pricing option provides the broadest eligible compute discount with the greatest flexibility?
options: Compute Savings Plans
EC2 Instance Savings Plans
Standard Reserved Instances for one EC2 configuration
Spot Instances for the entire required baseline
explanation:
Correct answer:
A. Compute Savings Plans apply to eligible EC2, Fargate, and Lambda usage. They retain broad flexibility across EC2 instance families, sizes, operating systems, tenancy, and Regions while the company commits to a consistent hourly spend.

Why the other options are wrong:
B. EC2 Instance Savings Plans are tied to an instance family in one Region and do not cover Fargate or Lambda.
C. Standard Reserved Instances apply to qualifying EC2 usage and are more configuration-specific; they do not cover Fargate or Lambda.
D. Spot capacity can be interrupted and is unsuitable as the only purchasing model for a mandatory baseline.

Exam trigger:
One compute commitment must follow EC2, Fargate, Lambda, and changing Regions.

Exam trap:
Compute Savings Plans maximise flexibility; EC2 Instance Savings Plans can offer a different discount level but have tighter scope.

Memory hook:
A flexible commitment across compute services means Compute Savings Plans.

question: A company runs predictable, always-on services as Fargate tasks and separate overnight Fargate batch tasks that are checkpointed and can tolerate interruption. Which TWO pricing strategies reduce cost without exposing the baseline services to interruption? (Select TWO.)
options: Purchase a Compute Savings Plan sized to the predictable Fargate baseline.
Run the fault-tolerant batch tasks on Fargate Spot.
Run all baseline services exclusively on Fargate Spot.
Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for the ECS services.
Move all container workloads to Dedicated Hosts.
explanation:
Correct answers:
A and B.

A. A Compute Savings Plan can discount predictable eligible Fargate usage while leaving the service on non-interruptible Fargate capacity.

B. Fargate Spot uses spare capacity at a discount and is appropriate for checkpointed tasks that can stop and retry.

Why the other options are wrong:
C. Fargate Spot interruptions could reduce the availability of the required baseline service.
D. DynamoDB reserved capacity does not apply to ECS or Fargate compute.
E. Dedicated Hosts are an EC2 licensing and isolation option and are not required for these managed Fargate workloads.

Exam trigger:
Stable Fargate baseline plus interruptible Fargate jobs requires a commitment for one and Spot for the other.

Exam trap:
Do not apply an interruption-tolerant purchasing model to the availability-critical baseline.

Memory hook:
Commit the baseline; Spot the retryable batch.

question: Log objects are read frequently for their first 30 days, infrequently for the following 60 days, and then retained for seven years. Retrieval after day 90 may take up to 12 hours. Which S3 Lifecycle design best matches the access pattern?
options: Store objects in S3 Standard, transition them to S3 Standard-IA after 30 days, and transition them to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days.
Store objects in S3 Glacier Deep Archive immediately after creation.
Keep every object in S3 Standard for all seven years.
Transition objects to S3 One Zone-IA after 30 days and delete them after 90 days.
explanation:
Correct answer:
A. S3 Standard supports frequent initial access. Standard-IA fits the subsequent infrequent-access period, and transitioning after 30 days satisfies its minimum storage-duration model. Glacier Deep Archive provides low-cost long-term retention when retrieval of archived data can take hours.

Why the other options are wrong:
B. Immediate Deep Archive storage cannot efficiently serve frequent reads during the first month.
C. S3 Standard meets the access requirement but wastes money during years of archival retention.
D. Deletion violates the seven-year requirement, and One Zone-IA provides less resilience than the multi-AZ storage classes.

Exam trigger:
Known hot, cool, and deep-archive phases point to an S3 Lifecycle policy.

Exam trap:
Account for storage-class minimum durations when choosing transition dates.

Memory hook:
Move data as its temperature falls.

question: Private subnets in multiple Availability Zones send large volumes of traffic to S3 and DynamoDB through one NAT gateway per Availability Zone. The workloads still require occasional IPv4 internet access to public software repositories, and the design must retain zonal egress resilience. Which TWO changes reduce recurring data-processing cost? (Select TWO.)
options: Create an S3 gateway VPC endpoint and associate it with the private-subnet route tables.
Create a DynamoDB gateway VPC endpoint and associate it with the private-subnet route tables.
Replace all NAT gateways with one NAT gateway in a single Availability Zone.
Create charged interface endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB in every subnet and remove all NAT gateways.
Route outbound repository traffic through a public Application Load Balancer.
explanation:
Correct answers:
A and B.

A. An S3 gateway endpoint adds private route-table entries for S3 and avoids NAT gateway processing for matching S3 traffic without hourly or endpoint data-processing charges.

B. A DynamoDB gateway endpoint provides the equivalent direct private route for DynamoDB traffic. The existing per-AZ NAT gateways can remain for resilient access to public repositories.

Why the other options are wrong:
C. One NAT gateway creates a zonal dependency and can add cross-AZ data-transfer cost for subnets in other Availability Zones.
D. Removing NAT gateways would break the required public IPv4 access, and interface endpoints introduce endpoint charges when free gateway endpoints satisfy the AWS-service traffic.
E. An ALB accepts inbound application traffic and is not a general outbound NAT service.

Exam trigger:
NAT cost is dominated by S3 and DynamoDB while internet egress is still required.

Exam trap:
Gateway endpoints remove AWS-service traffic from NAT; they do not replace NAT for arbitrary internet destinations.

Memory hook:
Give S3 and DynamoDB free gateway routes; keep zonal NAT for the internet.

question: A cloud-financial-management team needs recommendations for oversized EC2 instances and EBS volumes, checks for idle load balancers and unattached Elastic IP addresses, and historical cost and usage analysis. Which THREE services provide these capabilities? (Select THREE.)
options: AWS Compute Optimizer
AWS Trusted Advisor
AWS Cost Explorer
Amazon GuardDuty
AWS CloudTrail event history
AWS Shield Advanced
explanation:
Correct answers:
A, B, and C.

A. Compute Optimizer analyses utilisation and configuration data to produce rightsizing recommendations for supported resources, including EC2 instances and EBS volumes.

B. Trusted Advisor cost-optimisation checks can identify waste patterns such as underutilised resources, idle load balancers, and unattached Elastic IP addresses, depending on the account's support and service configuration.

C. Cost Explorer provides historical cost and usage analysis and supported rightsizing and commitment views.

Why the other options are wrong:
D. GuardDuty identifies threats rather than resource waste.
E. CloudTrail records API activity but is not a cost-rightsizing recommendation engine.
F. Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection.

Exam trigger:
Rightsizing recommendations, idle-resource checks, and spending analysis require complementary optimisation tools.

Exam trap:
No single listed service supplies every requested view.

Memory hook:
Optimizer sizes, Advisor checks, Explorer analyses spend.

question: A stateless nightly batch job saves checkpoints and can restart after an interruption. Which EC2 purchasing option is normally the most cost-effective?
options: Spot Instances
On-Demand Instances
Dedicated Hosts
Standard Reserved Instances
explanation:
Correct answer:
A. Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at a discount and are well suited to fault-tolerant, checkpointed workloads that can stop and resume.

Why the other options are wrong:
B. On-Demand avoids commitments but normally costs more when interruption is acceptable.
C. Dedicated Hosts are selected for host-level licensing, compliance, or isolation requirements rather than low-cost interruptible batch capacity.
D. Reserved Instances suit predictable EC2 baselines and require a commitment; they are not generally the lowest-cost choice for an interruption-tolerant intermittent job.

Exam trigger:
The job is restartable, checkpointed, and interruption tolerant.

Exam trap:
Spot saves cost only when the workload handles interruption correctly.

Memory hook:
Safe to interrupt means Spot.

question: A DynamoDB table is idle for long periods and receives irregular traffic bursts. The team cannot forecast capacity and wants minimal capacity administration without paying continuously for provisioned throughput. The expected bursts remain within the table's prepared on-demand scaling characteristics and quotas. Which capacity mode is the best fit?
options: On-demand capacity mode
Provisioned capacity fixed at the largest possible peak
Provisioned capacity without auto scaling
A reserved EC2 instance running an application cache
explanation:
Correct answer:
A. On-demand mode charges per request rather than for idle provisioned capacity and automatically manages throughput for variable workloads, subject to previous-peak behaviour, warm throughput, configured maximum throughput, and account quotas.

Why the other options are wrong:
B. Fixed peak provisioning incurs cost throughout long idle periods and still requires capacity forecasting.
C. Static provisioned capacity risks either persistent waste or throttling during bursts.
D. An EC2 cache does not replace DynamoDB write-capacity planning and adds infrastructure management.

Exam trigger:
Long idle periods, irregular demand, and minimal capacity management point to on-demand mode.

Exam trap:
On-demand is automatic but not an unlimited promise for an unprepared instantaneous increase far above prior demand.

Memory hook:
Irregular DynamoDB demand means on-demand.

question: Analysts run ad hoc SQL queries directly against files in S3 only a few times each month. The company does not want to provision or maintain a database or analytics cluster between query sessions. Which service is the most cost-effective fit?
options: Amazon Athena
An Amazon Redshift provisioned cluster
An Amazon EMR cluster that runs continuously
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with imported copies of the files
explanation:
Correct answer:
A. Athena is a serverless interactive query service that runs SQL directly against data in S3. The company pays for query processing rather than keeping a database or analytics cluster running between occasional sessions.

Why the other options are wrong:
B. A provisioned Redshift cluster creates ongoing capacity cost for an intermittent workload.
C. A continuously running EMR cluster is unnecessary for occasional ad hoc SQL.
D. Importing files into RDS adds data loading, storage, database sizing, patching, and administration.

Exam trigger:
Occasional serverless SQL directly over S3 points to Athena.

Exam trap:
Redshift is appropriate for sustained warehouse workloads; Athena is a strong fit for intermittent S3 queries.

Memory hook:
Ad hoc S3 SQL means Athena.

question: After authentication, one subscriber needs two hours of access to every private CloudFront object under /premium/*. Existing object URLs must remain unchanged, and the application should not generate an authorization token for every individual file. Which solution meets the requirements?
options: Issue CloudFront signed cookies with a custom policy that permits /premium/* until the expiration time.
Generate a separate CloudFront signed URL for every premium object.
Configure Origin Access Control and permit every viewer to access the distribution.
Return a separate regional S3 presigned URL for every object.
explanation:
Correct answer:
A. CloudFront signed cookies are intended for cases in which a viewer needs access to multiple restricted files or existing URLs must remain unchanged. A custom policy can use a wildcard resource path and an expiration condition to grant temporary access to /premium/*.

Why the other options are wrong:
B. Signed URLs are appropriate for individual resources, but issuing one per object adds unnecessary application work in this scenario.
C. Origin Access Control protects the S3 origin from direct access; it does not authenticate premium viewers at CloudFront.
D. S3 presigned URLs bypass the CloudFront private-content access design and still require a separate URL for each object.

Exam trigger:
Temporary access to many private CloudFront files without changing their URLs points to signed cookies.

Exam trap:
Origin Access Control secures the origin; signed cookies or URLs authorize viewers.

Memory hook:
Many protected files under one path mean signed cookies.
